Pashto has no standard written representation and no standard orthography; that Pashto is a very low resource, low-density language; and that Pashto speech translation requires a large number of customizations to standard ASR and MT systems.

(1) a written representation of a low-resource language is not necessarily an accurate representation of the spoken form, and that (2) speech recognition and speech synthesis systems for a low-resource language can be trained using a combination of a small amount of in-language data with large amounts of out-of-language data.

Pashto can be successfully represented with a modified Latin alphabet, that a corpus can be created for Pashto with a reasonable amount of effort, that the Pashto speech recognizer is robust enough to handle the variety of dialects and speakers in the corpus and to recognize words in the absence of a dictionary, that a speech synthesizer can be built for Pashto, and that an ASR system can be integrated with the speech translation system.
